skill.name: molfeat
skill.description: Use molfeat to convert SMILES or RDKit molecules into fingerprints, descriptors, and pretrained embeddings for QSAR, virtual screening, and molecular ML.
skill.summary: Guide molecular featurization workflows with molfeat for cheminformatics and machine learning.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline API names, local cache examples, and documentation links. No prompt injection attempt, data exfiltration intent, or automatic command execution was found. The only semantic concern is unsafe pickle cache loading guidance without a trust warning.

remediation.issue: Pickle cache examples do not warn users about trusted files.
remediation.suggestion: Add a warning to load pickle files only from trusted local caches, or recommend safer formats such as NumPy arrays or Parquet.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe Pickle Cache Loading in Examples
semantic_findings.description: The caching examples load embeddings from pickle files without warning that pickle files must be trusted. Copying this pattern for attacker-controlled cache files can enable code execution.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both examples use pickle.load on a local cache file. Exploitability depends on attacker control of that file, so the guidance risk is clear but contextual.

content.value_statement: Molecular ML projects need consistent features from SMILES and RDKit molecules. This skill guides molfeat choices, batch featurization, pretrained embeddings, caching, and QSAR workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains molfeat calculators, transformers, and pretrained molecular transformers.
Helps choose ECFP, MACCS, MAP4, RDKit descriptors, Mordred, ChemBERTa, GIN, and Graphormer features.
Shows batch featurization patterns for SMILES lists and RDKit molecule inputs.
Covers scikit-learn pipelines, cross-validation, grid search, and virtual screening workflows.
Describes ModelStore discovery for available pretrained featurizers.
Includes guidance for invalid SMILES handling, chunking, parallel processing, and embedding caches.
limitations: Requires molfeat, RDKit, and optional model dependencies to be installed separately.
Does not validate chemical datasets or model labels for scientific correctness.
Pretrained models may require downloads and compatible hardware or package versions.
Examples need adaptation before use in regulated or production research workflows.

use_cases.title: Prepare QSAR Features
use_cases.description: Select fingerprints or descriptors and build reproducible inputs for property prediction models.

use_cases.title: Build Screening Pipelines
use_cases.description: Convert large compound libraries into features for ranking, classification, and hit selection.

use_cases.title: Compare Molecular Embeddings
use_cases.description: Evaluate traditional fingerprints against pretrained embeddings for chemical similarity and model performance.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Featurizer
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose a molfeat featurizer for my SMILES dataset and explain the tradeoffs for QSAR modeling.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Batch Featurization
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a molfeat workflow for a large SMILES list with invalid molecule handling, parallel processing, and reproducible settings.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Model Inputs
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare ECFP, MACCS, RDKit descriptors, Mordred, and ChemBERTa features for my molecular prediction task.

prompt_templates.title: Design Screening Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a virtual screening plan using molfeat features, scikit-learn evaluation, ranking logic, and memory-conscious batch processing.

output_examples.input: I have 100,000 SMILES and need features for a property model.
output: Recommended starting with ECFP for speed and a strong baseline.
Suggested chunked batch processing with parallel workers to control memory use.
Outlined validation steps for invalid SMILES and reproducible featurizer settings.

output_examples.input: I want to compare ChemBERTa embeddings with classical descriptors.
output: Identified dependency and runtime differences for pretrained embeddings.
Proposed a comparison plan using the same train and validation splits.
Recommended tracking feature dimensions, runtime, and model metrics together.

output_examples.input: I need a similarity search workflow for a compound library.
output: Recommended ECFP or MAP4 depending on library size and similarity goals.
Explained how to compute query and library features consistently.
Suggested ranking top compounds after similarity scoring and review.

best_practices: Start with fast fingerprints before testing larger pretrained embeddings.
Save featurizer configuration and package versions for reproducible experiments.
Use chunking and parallel processing for large molecule collections.
anti_patterns: Do not compare featurizers using different train and validation splits.
Do not ignore invalid SMILES without tracking which molecules failed.
Do not use pretrained model caches from untrusted sources.

faq.question: What is molfeat used for?
faq.answer: Molfeat converts molecular structures into numerical features for machine learning, similarity search, and virtual screening.

faq.question: Can it work with SMILES strings?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples show SMILES inputs and RDKit molecule inputs for calculators and transformers.

faq.question: Does it include deep learning embeddings?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill covers pretrained transformers such as ChemBERTa, ChemGPT, GIN, and Graphormer models.

faq.question: Can I use it with scikit-learn?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill describes scikit-learn compatible transformers, pipelines, cross-validation, and grid search workflows.

faq.question: Does the skill install dependencies automatically?
faq.answer: No. It documents install commands and optional extras, but users must manage their environment.

faq.question: Is it safe for production workflows?
faq.answer: It is guidance for implementation. Review dependencies, cache handling, and scientific validation before production use.
